title: Finite-stage existence of classes for cohomology on colimit sites
statement: In the situation of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites] (a cofiltered $\mathcal I$, sites $\mathcal C_i$ with finite coverings, morphisms of sites $f_a$ given by $u_a$, the colimit site $\mathcal C$ with $f_i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C_i$ given by $u_i$), let $\mathcal F_i$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal C_i$ for every $i$, and for $a:j\to i$ let $\varphi_a:f_a^{-1}\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_j$ be a map of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C_j$, with $\varphi_c=\varphi_b\circ f_b^{-1}\varphi_a$ whenever $c=a\circ b$. The maps $f_j^{-1}\varphi_a:f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i=f_j^{-1}f_a^{-1}\mathcal F_i\to f_j^{-1}\mathcal F_j$ make $(f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i)$ a filtered system of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C$; set $\mathcal F=\varinjlim f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every i and X_i and p≥0 put A_t=H^p(u_{t.hom}(X_i), F_{t.right}) for t∈Under(i) (the filtered opposite-index convention). Let D:Under(i)→Ab have these objects and transitions given by pullback followed by H^p(φ), with transported endpoint equations as in Lean. Let c be the canonical cocone with target H^p(u_i(X_i), F) and legs κ_t given by canonical-site pullback followed by the coprojection into F, again with endpoint transports. For every y∈c.pt there exist t∈Under(i) and x∈D(t) with κ_t(x)=y.

source.place: Tag 09YP (lemma-colimit), with the right-exact diagram in Tag 0739; online copies at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09YP and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0739

proof.text: *The systems and the map.* Write $\mathcal I/i$ for the category of arrows $a:j\to i$ of $\mathcal I$ (a morphism $(a\circ b:k\to i)\to(a:j\to i)$ being $b:k\to j$); it is cofiltered because $\mathcal I$ is, so colimits over $(\mathcal I/i)^{\mathrm{op}}$ are filtered. For $a:j\to i$ and $b:k\to j$ put $\theta_b=H^p(\varphi_b)\circ f_b^*:H^p(u_a(X_i),\mathcal F_j)\to H^p(u_b u_a(X_i),f_b^{-1}\mathcal F_j)=H^p(u_{a\circ b}(X_i),f_b^{-1}\mathcal F_j)\to H^p(u_{a\circ b}(X_i),\mathcal F_k)$, with $f_b^*$ the pullback of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] (here $u_b\circ u_a=u_{a\circ b}$, [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites]). For $c:l\to k$, $\theta_c\circ\theta_b=H^p(\varphi_c)f_c^*H^p(\varphi_b)f_b^*=H^p(\varphi_c\circ f_c^{-1}\varphi_b)f_c^*f_b^*=H^p(\varphi_c\circ f_c^{-1}\varphi_b\circ c_{b,c}^{-1})(f_b\circ f_c)^*=H^p(\varphi_{b\circ c})f_{b\circ c}^*=\theta_{b\circ c}$ by naturality (2) and composition (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] and the cocycle condition (read through the canonical isomorphism $c_{b,c}:f_c^{-1}f_b^{-1}\cong f_{b\circ c}^{-1}$), so $(H^p(u_a(X_i),\mathcal F_j))_{a}$ is a functor on $(\mathcal I/i)^{\mathrm{op}}$. On $\mathcal C$ the transition maps of $(f_j^{-1}\mathcal F_j)$ are $\tau_b=f_k^{-1}\varphi_b\circ c:f_j^{-1}\mathcal F_j\cong f_k^{-1}f_b^{-1}\mathcal F_j\to f_k^{-1}\mathcal F_k$ ($f_b\circ f_k=f_j$ since $u_k\circ u_b=u_j$), with coprojections $\iota_j$ into $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Put $\kappa_a=H^p(\iota_j)\circ f_j^*:H^p(u_a(X_i),\mathcal F_j)\to H^p(u_ju_a(X_i),f_j^{-1}\mathcal F_j)=H^p(u_i(X_i),f_j^{-1}\mathcal F_j)\to H^p(u_i(X_i),\mathcal F)$. Then $\kappa_{a\circ b}\circ\theta_b=H^p(\iota_k)f_k^*H^p(\varphi_b)f_b^*=H^p(\iota_k\circ f_k^{-1}\varphi_b\circ c)f_j^*=H^p(\iota_k\circ\tau_b)f_j^*=\kappa_a$, again by (2) and (4). Hence the $\kappa_a$ induce the canonical map $\kappa:\varinjlim_{a:j\to i}H^p(u_a(X_i),\mathcal F_j)\to H^p(u_i(X_i),\mathcal F)$ of the statement. By (2) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] and the $\delta$-functor property of $H^\bullet(U,-)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\theta$ and $\kappa$ are natural in maps of systems $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_a)\to(\mathcal F'_i,\varphi'_a)$ and commute with the connecting maps of a short exact sequence of systems (one that is exact on every $\mathcal C_i$) and of the induced sequence of colimit sheaves on $\mathcal C$ when the latter is exact.

proof.text: *The case $p=0$.* $H^0(U,-)$ is $\Gamma(U,-)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and in degree $0$ the pullback $f_b^*$, resp. $f_j^*$, is the unit of $f_b^{-1}\dashv f_{b*}$, resp. $f_j^{-1}\dashv f_{j*}$, evaluated at the object ([lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] (1)). So the system $(H^0(u_a(X_i),\mathcal F_j),\theta_b)$ and the map $\kappa$ in degree $0$ are exactly the system $(\mathcal F_j(u_a(X_i)))$ and the map of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites-sections] (abelian version), which is an isomorphism. In degree zero, finite-stage representatives and finite-stage equality in filtered colimits give both class existence and eventual vanishing. This uses the inner-colimit formula 0A35 as well as the finite-covering section comparison: the current ColimitSiteSections declaration alone only handles a fixed sheaf diagram on the colimit site.

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 09YP, first paragraph: 'The case p = 0 is Sites, Lemma 09YN'

proof.text: *An injective system and a short exact sequence of systems.* By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites-injective-system] choose a system $(\mathcal G_i,\psi_a)$ of injective abelian sheaves with an injective map of systems $\gamma:(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_a)\to(\mathcal G_i,\psi_a)$. Let $\mathcal Q_i=\operatorname{Coker}(\gamma_i)$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C_i)$. Since $f_a^{-1}$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $f_a^{-1}\mathcal Q_i=\operatorname{Coker}(f_a^{-1}\gamma_i)$, and since $\psi_a\circ f_a^{-1}\gamma_i=\gamma_j\circ\varphi_a$, the map $\psi_a$ induces $\chi_a:f_a^{-1}\mathcal Q_i\to\mathcal Q_j$; the cocycle condition $\chi_{a\circ b}=\chi_b\circ f_b^{-1}\chi_a$ holds because it holds for $\psi$ and $f_{a\circ b}^{-1}\mathcal G_i\to f_{a\circ b}^{-1}\mathcal Q_i$ is an epimorphism. Thus $0\to(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_a)\to(\mathcal G_i,\psi_a)\to(\mathcal Q_i,\chi_a)\to0$ is a sequence of systems, exact on every $\mathcal C_i$, and the maps $\varphi_b$, $\psi_b$, $\chi_b$ form a map of short exact sequences $f_b^{-1}(0\to\mathcal F_j\to\mathcal G_j\to\mathcal Q_j\to0)\to(0\to\mathcal F_k\to\mathcal G_k\to\mathcal Q_k\to0)$. Applying the exact functors $f_i^{-1}$ gives a filtered system (over $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$) of short exact sequences $0\to f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i\to f_i^{-1}\mathcal G_i\to f_i^{-1}\mathcal Q_i\to0$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, and since filtered colimits in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ are exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact], $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal Q\to0$ is exact, where $\mathcal G=\varinjlim f_i^{-1}\mathcal G_i$, $\mathcal Q=\varinjlim f_i^{-1}\mathcal Q_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 09YP, second paragraph ('Choose (F_i, phi_a) -> (G_i, psi_a) as in Lemma 0EXZ'), with the short exact sequences of the proof of Lemma Tag 0739 (lemma-colim-works-over-collection: 'Since colimits of sheaves are the sheafification of colimits on the level of presheaves, since sheafification is exact, and since filtered colimits of abelian groups are exact')

proof.text: *Vanishing for colimits of injective systems.* Let $(\mathcal G_i,\psi_a)$ be any system as in the statement with every $\mathcal G_i$ an injective abelian sheaf, and $\mathcal G=\varinjlim f_i^{-1}\mathcal G_i$. We show $H^q(U,\mathcal G)=0$ for all $U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $q>0$. Let $\mathcal U$ be any covering of $\mathcal C$. By the definition of $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$ [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites] there are $i$ and a (finite) covering $\mathcal U_i$ of $\mathcal C_i$ with $\mathcal U=u_i(\mathcal U_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites-cech-complex], $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\cong\varinjlim_{a:j\to i}\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(u_a(\mathcal U_i),\mathcal G_j)$, a filtered colimit of complexes, where $u_a(\mathcal U_i)$ is a covering of $\mathcal C_j$. Each $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(u_a(\mathcal U_i),\mathcal G_j)$ is exact in degrees $q>0$ since $\mathcal G_j$ is injective [lem-weil-pbc-site-injective-cech-acyclic]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] to the sequences $\check{\mathcal C}^{q-1}\to\check{\mathcal C}^q\to\check{\mathcal C}^{q+1}$ ($q\ge1$), the colimit complex is exact in degrees $q>0$, i.e. $\check H^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=0$ for $q>0$ [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion] to $\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $\mathrm{Cov}=\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$: hypothesis (1) holds trivially (all fibre products of members of a covering exist, being objects of $\mathcal C$), (2) holds since every covering is in $\mathrm{Cov}$, (3) was just shown. Hence $H^q(U,\mathcal G)=0$ for all $q>0$ and all $U$.

proof.text: Induct simultaneously over all systems in the degree, establishing the two finite-stage assertions in smaller degrees by steps 1–4. In degree n+1, take a class y on the colimit site. The long exact sequence and positive acyclicity of the colimit of G lift it to z in H^n of the colimit of the cokernel system R. By degree-n stage existence, z comes from z_t at a stage. Its stage connecting image maps to y by compatibility with connecting maps. Transport by hDobj and hclegs to obtain x in D(t) with c_t(x)=y. No uniqueness or detection assertion in degree n+1 is used.
